title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Release acceptance journey
text:
Release acceptance journey
Provision two synthetic companies, differently scoped branches/operators and qualified Android TV devices. Verify API/media/catalog allow/deny cases and no implicit support privilege.
Pair devices, create a cross-branch group and an explicit individual exception. Upload media; configure a custom weekly-agenda catalog and product/price configuration. Compose independent and coordinated areas, regional schedules and an optional default; preview and publish A.
Verify local multi-video/audio/catalog rendering under the qualified profile. Edit drafts without changing A. Save a price and verify automatic consistent publication from published dependencies without leaking unrelated drafts; test concurrent edits, duplicate delivery and failed/unknown outcomes.
Publish B while playback continues. Cut network/power at download/staging/activation boundaries and verify complete valid A or B. Isolate a runtime regional fault without confusing it with incomplete-generation activation. Check protected references and insufficient disk outcomes.
Exercise schedule/date/DST/promotion/no-match/pagination and regional-page timing offline. Test the trusted-clock and authorization deadlines, restart/recovery and the expected safe neutral states.
Reconnect and reconcile observed state. Unlink/revoke while offline, then verify cleanup before cross-company pairing. Exercise historical recovery without expired offers or resurrected credentials and validate controlled protocol/app updates.
Rehearse database-plus-media restore and endpoint migration in isolation. Record target-linked load/usability/hardware evidence, costs and residual risk before real-customer acceptance.
Evidence includes automated contract/security/integration/browser tests, representative hardware/power/network tests, restore results and user observation. Delivery can be incremental; an operational release requires the complete applicable acceptance set. Passing foundation validation only checks currently implemented foundation/docs.

title: Teluni Initial Release Requirements and Acceptance
heading: Explicitly outside the MVP
text:
Explicitly outside the MVP
The historical heading remains a stable route; initial scope now includes freeform composition, configurable catalogs and their approved commercial defaults. Further unreviewed widgets, managed campaigns, external ERP/POS/partner integration APIs/webhooks/imports, automated billing/subscriptions, white-label, AI, playback analytics, general remote support, synchronization across separate screens and alternative players remain future unless independently approved. Generic fields do not approve arbitrary executable plugins, unrestricted data collection or all roadmap capabilities.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Constraints and current state
text:
Constraints and current state
**Decided constraint:** no present cloud-service budget. The owner intends to use a personal residential server for development, tests and potentially initial customers, moving to a VPS/cloud when revenue or operational need justifies it. **Proposed technology:** Debian Linux, Docker Compose, a reverse proxy with HTTPS, local persistent media, automated backups and suitable monitoring. None is a deployed Teluni environment or executable procedure in this repository.
Follow inherited [production access](../security/production-access.md), [secrets management](../security/secrets-management.md), [retention](../security/data-retention.md), [observability](../reliability/observability.md), [alerting](../reliability/alerting.md), and [runbook authoring](../runbooks/authoring.md). This plan does not grant production authority. Write tested deployment/recovery runbooks when the environment exists, rather than speculative commands now.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Residential exposure and readiness gate
text:
Residential exposure and readiness gate
[PH-10](human-actions.md#ph-10) requires an actual host/network inventory: CPU/RAM/disk and growth, upload bandwidth, data caps, power/reboot recovery, router/firewall, public address or CGNAT, ISP restrictions, available domain, certificate renewal, secure remote administration and backup connectivity. Keep private addresses, credentials and sensitive topology out of tracked public documentation.
A tunnel, free DNS option or any video-delivery intermediary requires evaluation of current terms, limits, privacy, security, transfer cost and failure behavior before selection. Do not assume Cloudflare Tunnel, DNS, or video distribution automatically provides an acceptable production path. No such provider is selected here.
Before any real pilot, record and demonstrate:
HTTPS works end to end; only intentional public application endpoints are exposed. PostgreSQL, orchestration dashboards and administrative interfaces remain private/restricted. Remote administration does not imply an unrestricted remote-control product feature.
Development/test and customer data, identities, credentials and backups are separated; logs/diagnostics are redacted; real data does not enter development fixtures.
Durable database and media survive container recreation, controlled app updates and host reboot. Schema migrations use reviewed release procedures and an explicit recovery plan.
Offline playback has been tested independently from backend availability. A home outage still prevents new uploads, publication, pairing, current monitoring and some recovery; communicate these limits to pilot participants.
The owner agrees measurable availability, maintenance, incident contact, backup RPO/RTO and support expectations. No commercial SLA is implied by the architecture.
Until verified, external exposure and real-customer operation are **pending**, even if development works locally.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Persistent state and storage portability
text:
Persistent state and storage portability
Keep environment-specific URLs, credentials and paths in validated environment configuration; use only implemented keys from the [configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md) today. Define and document new keys with their future canonical schemas when implemented. Do not embed the residential hostname/path in business entities, contracts or player binaries.
**Proposed storage boundary:** the media capability owns object identity, integrity, metadata, authorized reads and lifecycle. Isolate the actual filesystem I/O behind a cohesive media-owned storage responsibility so a future S3-compatible implementation can preserve object semantics without rewriting domain rules. Avoid a general provider framework or mandatory S3 dependency now. Object-store replacement still needs verified access, integrity, migration and concurrency semantics; portability is not a free automatic migration.
Use durable logical object identifiers rather than storing temporary download credentials as business identity. External media endpoints are configurable. Authorized delivery may use an API or another reviewed access mechanism; public filesystem paths and unbounded permanent bearer URLs are not the default.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Backup and restore requirements
text:
Backup and restore requirements
Backups must cover PostgreSQL, media and the non-secret configuration/release metadata needed to reconstruct operation. Protect and recover secrets through a separate controlled process. A database-only backup is insufficient if it points to unavailable media.
Choose a consistency method for the database-plus-files set, backup schedule, off-host destination, encryption/key recovery, retention, capacity and success/failure reporting. A second directory on the same disk does not cover loss of the host. Local budget constraints do not eliminate the need to resolve off-host recovery before accepting private customer data.
Rehearse restore into an isolated environment: verify migration/application compatibility, ownership/permissions, manifest-to-file integrity, representative playback and tenant access, then reconcile revoked identities and deletion/retention obligations. Record achieved recovery point/time and compare them with owner-approved RPO/RTO. Preserve audit/release history; do not restore stale authorization silently.

title: Teluni Deployment and Migration Planning
heading: Future host or storage migration
text:
Future host or storage migration
**Proposed sequence**, to turn into tested runbooks once topology and credentials exist:
Inventory supported player versions, configurable API/media addresses, tenant data, assets, release versions and secret destinations. Prepare DNS/certificate ownership and compatible software at the destination.
Rehearse backup restore and file verification without customer writes. Determine whether logical object IDs remain stable and how private media authorization is preserved.
Plan a bounded write cutover or verified incremental reconciliation to avoid divergent metadata and media. Preserve audit and device identities without exposing their credentials.
Update endpoints through the approved mechanism with certificate validation and rollback capability. Keep the old address/redirect or compatibility path only for an explicitly defined overlap, accounting for long-offline players. Never accept arbitrary redirected credential recipients.
Verify representative players reconnect, reconcile desired/active versions, and continue offline playback. Check uploads, access denial, publication, backups and monitoring on the new host.
Close the rollback window deliberately, reconcile retained data/deletions and retire old storage/credentials safely. The endpoint overlap and maximum supported offline interval must be compatible; unresolved unreachable devices require a support plan.
Triggers for migration include measured cost/availability/support risk, storage or uplink saturation, growth, or earned revenue supporting operations. Cloud procurement and live migration are outside this documentation task.

text:
Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
[Requirements](mvp.md) · [Release policies](release-policies.md) · [Acceptance targets](release-targets.md) · [ADR-0019 proposal](../adr/0019-propose-immutable-publications-and-atomic-player-activation.md)

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Required guarantees and proposal boundary
text:
Required guarantees and proposal boundary
**Decided requirements:** local media and catalog rendering through the bounded offline envelope, integrity validation, complete-generation activation and last-valid recovery. Normal video playback does not stream repeatedly from the backend. Freeform composition, independently scheduled areas with optional page coordination, multiple videos/audio and typed custom catalogs must meet the same obligations.
PH-09 has selected product behavior and numeric qualification targets. Protocol/schema serialization, integrity metadata/algorithms, local transactions/storage, processing/rendering libraries, transport and credential/trusted-time mechanisms remain engineering review under D-03/D-04/D-05/D-07/D-11. [ADR-0023](../adr/0023-propose-versioned-catalog-and-composition-publications.md) proposes the versioned catalog/composition boundary; neither ADR is an implemented protocol or evidence of durability.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Publication lifecycle
text:
Publication lifecycle
An authorized publisher deliberately publishes ordinary draft state. A designated price save instead automatically records publication intent for affected published bindings under the release policies; it does not release unrelated layout/schema/record drafts.
Validate actor/target tenant and branch scope, schema/record/field bindings, compatible rendering/media profiles, scheduling, effective prices and durable media. Build an immutable complete snapshot with the rules/data needed for offline interpretation. Desired availability must not precede durable assets and metadata.
Record the desired generation and required work durably. A database update and media filesystem writes are not one transaction. Stage/verify objects, then commit references/intent with recoverable cleanup and reconciliation. Follow delivery policy; an in-memory after-commit callback alone cannot guarantee price/publication fan-out.
The independently authenticated device reconciles its authorized desired generation and local active/staged state. It receives only compatible tenant-scoped rules, schema/record snapshots and media descriptors. A content path is not immutable identity when its bytes can change.
Preflight space for staged plus protected active/recovery resources and the target reserve, counting shared files once. Download absent/changed assets with bounded timeouts/retries. Interrupted files cannot masquerade as complete; refreshing download authorization cannot make private media public.
Verify expected length/integrity, references, schema interpretation and renderer/media capability before accepting resources. A checksum detects corruption but does not authenticate an untrusted manifest by itself. Preserve valid active output on invalid or incomplete staging.
Prepare the complete supported local generation, then durably activate it. Keep publication selection distinct from the schedule that chooses its eligible output. Atomic-generation recovery and safe resource release need actual power-cut tests; do not overwrite active files progressively.
Report desired, received/staged and reported-active facts separately. Repeated/lost acknowledgements must reconcile; server acceptance is not proof of TV activation. The panel represents active A plus failed staging B without calling every sync failure a playback outage.
Retain the previous valid generation and protected staging resources under retention/reference rules. Restore only if still authorized, compatible and commercially valid. Do not resurrect expired promotions, deleted ownership or revoked credentials.
Confirmed assignment/source changes use the latest published programming without another content publish action. An explicitly confirmed destination with no first publication produces authorized neutral no-programming output after the assignment is applied. This deliberate empty source differs from failed/corrupt synchronization, which preserves valid state. An unreachable player cannot apply an unseen assignment or erasure.
Candidate logical states such as unpaired, no-content, staging, active, degraded and pending-clear describe concurrent facts, not committed enum/API names. Their exact schema must preserve the distinctions above.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Consistency and concurrency
text:
Consistency and concurrency
Publication/price-save/download/acknowledgement operations need explicit idempotency, stale-write detection, retry ownership, bounded attempts and observable failure/reconciliation. Do not treat a mutation timeout as certain failure or retry an unprotected side effect.
Order desired state using authoritative generation/revision information, not device wall-clock order. Old acknowledgements and stale processing cannot roll a target back to an earlier price or assignment.
Under the owner's delegation, prefer the latest authorized compatible desired snapshot and permit coalescing superseded pending delivery work. Keep attributable publication/price history and every still-valid schedule in the latest snapshot; coalescing delivery is not deleting audit events or omitting future programmed transitions.
Use published dependency revisions for automatic price publication. Concurrent schema/layout drafts remain separate. Expose saved/queued/publication-failed states, reconcile incomplete fan-out and never claim successful device distribution from the catalog transaction alone.
Typed schema evolution/import and reference validation are part of publication validity. A record/field reference cannot bypass tenant/branch authorization or select another tenant through a custom value.
Retry elapsed time is separate from business scheduling. Respect application shutdown and bounded work claims; a crashed worker must not lose required intent or leave inaccessible staging permanently.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Time and regional scheduling
text:
Time and regional scheduling
[Release policies](release-policies.md#time-and-scheduling) own the exact calendar/DST/overnight/date-clipping and conflict rules. Backend preview and player must share fixtures for them, regional overrides/page coordination, promotional price validity, pagination and no-match output. Store/compare instants while retaining the geographic zone needed for recurring local time; never inherit the backend host timezone.
An active regional schedule controls its area's output even while the underlying page changes. On ending, return to the applicable current-page/default/neutral state without restarting independent areas. Coordinated page-controlled participants use a common transition point; ordinary short-video completion holds the last frame while the page continues. Schedule boundaries interrupt affected output and override fades/page/item completion without extending expired content.
A regional rendering failure inside an active valid generation may use its still-valid local contingency or neutral area and report degradation while other areas continue. This runtime isolation does not permit activation of a publication with missing/corrupt required resources. A recovered coordinated area rejoins the current valid page/schedule state; it does not replay expired content or reset every area.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Authorization, clock and recovery boundaries
text:
Authorization, clock and recovery boundaries
The [target specification](release-targets.md#reliability-and-synchronization-targets) defines offline authorization and trusted-clock limits. Authorization expiry gives neutral output and requires reconnection; a restored cache cannot extend it. Server revocation rejects new protected operations while a disconnected cache may persist until local authorization expires. Erasure is pending until actually observed, and another tenant cannot pair before verified cleanup/reset.
Detectable clock jumps or insufficient trusted-time confidence suspend time-dependent schedules/prices. Do not claim an incorrect wall clock can always be detected without a reference. If remaining authorization validity cannot be established safely, protected playback must also stop; a local setup/neutral view does not disclose private tenant data. Reboot/offline time estimation and established credential/cryptographic components require threat-model review and qualified tests before delivery.
Initial pairing/synchronization requires backend access. With no valid installed program show safe local setup/no-content output. A publication's optional default or neutral fallback is evaluated locally within authorization and content-validity rules, not permission to replay stale commercial data indefinitely.

title: Teluni Offline Playback and Synchronization
heading: Failure and recovery acceptance
text:
Failure and recovery acceptance
Condition
Required observable outcome / evidence
Server/network outage after sync
Local media/catalog/region scheduling continues within AT-10/AT-15/AT-16; verify expected neutral state at expiry/uncertain time
Interrupted download or expired access
Safe bounded retry/resume only when verified; active generation continues; no partial asset activation
Invalid schema, binding, manifest, media or incompatible profile
Reject staging with bounded actionable diagnostics; keep active valid output; no infinite hot retry or cross-tenant reference
Insufficient storage/memory
Respect AT-05, refuse unsafe preparation and preserve active/recovery assets; do not remove functions silently
Power/process failure at prepare/switch
Recover a complete eligible generation and reconcile partial/orphan staging; qualify AT-06–AT-10 on representative devices
Duplicate/reordered/concurrent price/publication work
Reconcile idempotently; exclude unrelated drafts, stale-price rollback and mixed generations
Regional runtime failure or no-match
Isolate the affected output under policy, retain other geometry/output and report actual degradation
Date/DST/clock/promotion boundary
Preview/player fixture agreement and AT-13/AT-16; never revive expired output through fallback or rollback
Revoked/unlinked/unreachable device
Reject future protected access; enforce local authorization deadline; distinguish pending/confirmed erasure and require cleanup before reassignment
Incompatible generation or failed player update
Follow AT-26 support window; preserve allowed playback, report incompatibility, use qualified update/rollback recovery
Host move or database/media restore
Reconcile device intent, ownership/revocation and publication resources in an isolated rehearsal; never leak credentials or point devices at an untested recovery endpoint
Every interruption boundary needs automated contract/security fixtures and physical hardware/network/power evidence, not only happy-path mocks. All future product target measurements remain pending. PH-08/PJ-12/PJ-14 own device qualification; PH-10/PJ-13 own host/restore/migration readiness.

title: Teluni Product Vision
heading: Purpose and positioning
text:
Purpose and positioning
**Decided:** Teluni is a multi-tenant digital signage SaaS for centralized management of visual content on televisions, monitors, and other display devices. It should combine simple operation, reliable local playback, freeform simultaneous presentation and configurable data-driven content. Brazil is the initial market, with international commercialization anticipated. The owner selected initial capabilities for product quality rather than limiting them solely by the MVP label.
Locale
Intended slogan
`pt-BR`
Todas as suas telas. Um só lugar.
`en-US`
Every screen. One place.
**Decided:** the owner approved Teluni as the product name and `teluni.app` as the principal domain. `teluni.com.br` is the secondary/defensive Brazil option (availability reported by the owner); unavailable/premium `teluni.com` is outside the current budget and scope. [Branding](branding/README.md) owns these decisions and the approved Connected Tiles identity. Preliminary trademark research has advanced, but registration/control and final clearance are not inferred. Connected Tiles is integrated into the web shell, portal and favicon, with the selected locally served font and derived touch icon. [PH-07](human-actions.md#ph-07) remains in progress for domain registration/control and trademark evidence.

title: Teluni Product Vision
heading: Origin and pilot
text:
Origin and pilot
The initial opportunity is a snack bar considering televisions for products, images, videos, and promotions. It is a candidate pilot, not a confirmed customer or an exclusive definition of the product.
The owner's experience with PDT Display provides conceptual learning only. Teluni must have independent architecture, identity, and implementation. Do not copy PDT Display code, assets, credentials, customer data, private designs, or proprietary information without authorization. Authorized Orion material remains governed by the repository's provenance and license. The owner selected Apache-2.0 for Teluni source and documentation; [ADR-0022](../adr/0022-license-teluni-under-apache-2-0.md) records that decision and [PH-06](human-actions.md#ph-06) records its verification. SaaS pricing and customer terms remain separate commercial decisions.

title: Teluni Product Vision
heading: Actors and core journeys
text:
Actors and core journeys
The [security model](security-and-i18n.md#actors-and-authorization) defines proposed privileges. The product journeys are:
A platform administrator establishes a customer company and its initial company administrator.
A company administrator creates branches and delegates permitted operations to members.
An authorized operator pairs a display using a temporary code shown by the player and assigns it to the correct branch.
An authorized publisher uploads media, configures typed catalogs/fields/records (for example products or a weekly agenda), composes regional content/schedules, previews and publishes.
Authorized price saves automatically publish affected already-published data bindings, without releasing unrelated drafts or recreating artwork. Other draft edits retain explicit publication.
The player stages complete consistent versions and continues local media/catalog rendering through the selected offline/clock envelope, with independent areas or optional coordinated pages.
A scoped operator sees last contact, synchronization progress and actionable failures without unrestricted remote access. Actual player observation is distinct from server intent.
Acceptance of these journeys is specified in [MVP requirements](mvp.md); the exact enrollment and permission policies remain review items there.

title: Teluni Product Vision
heading: Commercial hypotheses
text:
Commercial hypotheses
**Decided:** recurring SaaS is the intended business model. **Proposed:** charge primarily by number of screens, potentially with a company minimum and feature-based plans. BRL 79.90/month for up to two screens is an exploratory price only, not an approved offer, entitlement, tax treatment, or billing rule.
Prices, plans, storage/traffic/processing limits, support hours, installation fees, cancellation, costs, and partner/referral arrangements require [PH-12](human-actions.md#ph-12). The snack bar pilot should provide evidence of usability, reliability, support demand, willingness to pay, and actual costs. Automatic billing and payment-gateway integration are **future**, not MVP prerequisites. International currencies and presentation follow the [localization requirements](security-and-i18n.md#internationalization).
There is currently no cloud-service budget. Residential hosting is an entry proposal with explicit [operational gates and risks](operations.md), not a commitment to production availability.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Teluni Release Policies
text:
Teluni Release Policies
[Requirements](mvp.md) · [Acceptance targets](release-targets.md) · [Playback and synchronization](playback-and-sync.md) · [PH-09](human-actions.md#ph-09)

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Decision status and ownership
text:
Decision status and ownership
**Decided on 2026-10-18:** these product policies consolidate the owner's questionnaire and the remaining choices explicitly delegated to engineering. They extend the earlier company-to-screen requirements to freeform composition and configurable catalogs. Product capability and quality take priority over reducing scope solely for an MVP label. None of these decisions proves implementation, hardware capacity or release readiness.
This document owns observable business behavior. [Acceptance targets](release-targets.md) own numeric limits and qualification goals; [playback/sync](playback-and-sync.md) owns the proposed delivery lifecycle; [architecture](architecture.md#pending-decisions) and ADRs own remaining technical choices. PH-08/PH-10/PH-11/PH-13 and PJ-07 retain their separate hardware, operations, identity, privacy and architecture reviews.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Assignment and publication
text:
Assignment and publication
Support individual-device assignment and persistent company-owned groups. A device belongs to zero or one programming group; a group may span authorized branches of the same company. Check all target references and permissions on the server.
A grouped device follows its group unless an authorized user explicitly selects individual programming. That choice replaces the complete group programming, retains membership and is visibly identified in the panel. Returning to the group is explicit; a membership edit does not silently remove the exception.
Confirming an assignment/source change requests the destination's latest published programming without another publish action. An intentionally unpublished destination is permitted after a clear pre-confirmation indication: after applying the authorized change, the player shows local neutral output until its first valid publication. A failed or unseen synchronization instead preserves valid state.
Ordinary layout, schema, record, playlist and schedule edits are drafts until deliberately published. An exception applies to an authorized **price save**: it automatically records publication intent for affected published bindings and produces a new validated version. A price save never mutates a snapshot in place or publishes unrelated drafts. This exception concerns designated monetary price semantics, not every numeric/custom field.
Distinguish saved, queued, failed, published, downloaded and active states. If automatic price publication fails, show the pending/failure state and retry/reconcile durably; do not report that disconnected TVs have changed. Duplicate saves/retries and concurrent edits must not replay an obsolete price over a newer one. Invalid input is rejected before accepting a price change.
A publication contains consistent layout/schema/record/price/media versions. Activation requires its complete supported resource set; failure preserves the last valid generation. Rollback still applies current authorization and content-validity rules and cannot resurrect an expired promotion.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Configurable catalogs
text:
Configurable catalogs
Catalogs are tenant-owned, user-configurable collections with typed field definitions and records. They are not restricted to product tables or a fixed mandatory set of product fields. Users can add fields and define required/optional values; products, menus and public weekly agendas are examples of reusable configurations. A weekly-agenda record describes displayed data and does not implicitly become a player publication schedule.
Provide reviewed field types for text, numbers, booleans, dates/times, selections, monetary values, authorized media and scoped record references as appropriate. Exact type schemas and storage remain technical design work. Validate field definitions, values, references, sizes and nesting. Customization does not permit arbitrary code, SQL, executable markup or unrestricted external data access, and does not imply unbounded resources.
Stable field identity and schema versions must preserve bindings. Renaming a label must not silently change meaning. A destructive schema/type change needs explicit migration/reference handling; published versions remain bound to their original validated schema and values. Importing/copying layouts or catalog definitions does not grant access to another company's media or records.
Product configurations can use description/image/category/availability, normal/promotional monetary values and variation/combo references without imposing those fields on an agenda or another catalog. This defines extensible data and presentation, not an ERP/POS transaction engine. Ordinary catalog edits retain draft/publication separation; designated price updates use the automatic publication exception above.
**Delegated commercial defaults:** a company-level base price may be overridden by branch. Every monetary value has explicit currency and exact representation; do not convert currencies automatically. Preview the effective branch value. A promotional price applies only within its published validity, then falls back to the normal price. Reject competing promotion periods for the same product/branch. Hide unavailable products by default; a component may explicitly show an unavailable indication instead. All of these rules must be evaluable from a valid offline publication.
Catalog views bind selected fields into a list/table/menu/agenda rather than relying only on flattened artwork. Support automatic pagination with configurable timing, grouping by an available chosen field and an explicit minimum readable text size, plus manual pagination. Never silently clip names/prices or shrink text indefinitely; an unresolvable overflow needs visible validation. Generic catalogs need no mandatory category or price field.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Composition and regional playback
text:
Composition and regional playback
Provide a freeform editor to create, position and resize simultaneous areas. A group is a programming source, not a limit on area count. Validate geometry, orientation, references and the supported rendering profile; do not silently drop a function to fit a device.
Layouts have a structured, versioned textual representation with validated copy/import/export, revision history and preview. Serialization, editor/renderer libraries and wire schemas remain subject to technical review; AI is not required.
Areas advance independently by default, with optional coordinated areas/pages. This owner-approved hybrid mode replaces compulsory whole-screen progression while retaining that capability when selected. Coordination within one TV does not approve synchronization across separate TVs.
Each area may have its own schedules and optional default. Its active schedule selects the area's content and is not overwritten by a global page transition. After the exception ends, return to the current page's applicable content, then its configured default, otherwise a neutral area; do not restart unrelated independent areas. Preview must expose these regional exceptions to page coordination. Coordinated page changes use one transition point for the participating page-controlled areas; a regional exception temporarily keeps its own eligible output.
When no schedule or default applies, keep that area's geometry and neutral background without automatically redistributing the layout. A complete programming source with no eligible output uses safe local no-programming output. Never borrow a group default while an individual override is selected.
Coordinated pages have explicit duration, with an automatic suggestion covering the longest video. Reject ordinary page durations that would cut a full video. Shorter videos finish and hold their last frame until the page changes; static content remains visible. Independent areas retain their per-item durations. Scheduled boundaries override ordinary completion and may interrupt any current item/page.
Support several concurrent videos subject to a measured device profile. Ordinary video playback uses its complete original duration; per-item trimming is not part of the selected baseline. Independent image items use the default/configurable bounds in the target specification.
Support individual audio mute/volume controls and multiple audible areas. **Delegated safe default:** newly created areas start muted and mixed audio requires deliberate configuration; do not impose a universal one-audio-area limit. Qualification must test the supported mix, output controls and recovery.
During an already-active presentation, isolate a rendering failure to its area: attempt bounded recovery, then show still-valid regional contingency content or neutral output, preserve unaffected areas and report the failure. Keep a coordinated group's logical page timeline; a failed area may rejoin at the current valid state instead of forcing every area to restart. Whole-generation staging/integrity failures remain distinct and preserve the previous valid generation.
Offer direct cuts and configurable fades with preview only on validated profiles. A fade never extends expired commercial content; when necessary at an expiry boundary use an immediate cut. Advanced effects remain separate scope.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Time and scheduling
text:
Time and scheduling
Use per-device local business time: explicit device timezone, otherwise the deliberately selected branch timezone. Never inherit the server host timezone. Cross-branch groups therefore interpret local recurring hours per target. Locale changes do not change timing.
Start instants are inclusive and end instants exclusive. Reject overlapping schedules competing for the same output/area; intentional concurrent content in different areas is permitted. Do not resolve conflicts by implicit priority, last edit or creation order. Backend preview and player must share fixtures.
Permit overnight windows anchored to the starting weekday: Friday 22:00–02:00 ends Saturday at 02:00. Date-only final validity includes that complete local day and ends at the next local midnight, clipping any overnight window at that limit. If Friday is the last valid day, its 22:00–02:00 window therefore ends at Saturday 00:00. Reject equal start/end times as ambiguous and provide a separate explicit all-day option.
Follow geographic timezone rules. For nonexistent local boundaries use the first valid instant; for ambiguous boundaries use the earlier occurrence for a start and the later occurrence for an end. Show the resolved result in preview, validate conflicts after resolving it and do not duplicate publication/execution solely because clocks repeat. Exact library/fixture implementation remains technical work.
When eligible scheduled output changes, interrupt the current item instead of waiting for completion. Apply this to the affected regional output or page-controlled coordinated participants; an unrelated independent area continues. Timing tolerances and trusted-clock bounds are defined in the acceptance targets, not claimed measurements.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Media and deletion lifecycle
text:
Media and deletion lifecycle
The acceptance targets define configurable ingestion bounds separately from supported playback profiles and commercial quotas. Validate declared and inspected file type, size, decoded dimensions, duration, compatibility and scoped references; exact allowed codecs/containers require D-05 review.
Preserve originals and create compatible renditions when validated processing is supported. Show preparation/progress/preview and keep publications unavailable until their required renditions are durable. If safe conversion is unavailable, reject with an actionable reason. Do not silently remove areas or distort content to compensate for an unsupported device. Processing isolation/tools/capacity remain technical and host-readiness work.
Archiving removes media from new selections but does not break existing references. Block physical deletion while referenced by drafts, active/staged/recovery generations or protected retained publications; disclose only references the caller may see. Assisted removal of draft references needs confirmation and never rewrites issued snapshots. Retention expiration alone is insufficient for garbage collection: reference protection, device reconciliation and the offline envelope must also permit removal.
Keep active and previous valid player generations plus valid staging resources. Preflight new resources and the reserved-space target; insufficient capacity preserves valid playback and reports required capacity rather than deleting protected resources. Deduplicate shared immutable assets when accounting for generations. Catalog schema/record/media references need the same reference-aware lifecycle; legal/privacy retention remains PH-13.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Offline authorization and clock trust
text:
Offline authorization and clock trust
The target specification fixes the maximum offline authorization interval and clock-uncertainty bound. After authorization expires, show neutral output and request reconnection. Revocation denies new protected server operations; an unreachable device may retain playback until its local authorization expires. Do not claim remote erasure while unreachable or extend authorization by restoring an older generation.
Detectable incompatible clock jumps or insufficient trusted time suspend time-dependent schedules/prices and produce neutral output with diagnostics. Do not guess promotional validity or claim all wrong clocks can be detected without a reference. Elapsed-time retries and business wall-clock time are separate. Reboot/offline trusted-time estimation and credential mechanisms require threat-model/technical review using established security components.
Unlink requires explicit authorized confirmation, server revocation and a distinct pending-clear state for offline devices. On reconnection clear private local content/configuration/credentials. Reassignment to another company requires verified cleanup or controlled reset before new pairing. Distinguish revoked access, unreachable device and confirmed erasure; failure/retry must never expose the previous tenant's data.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Compatibility and updates
text:
Compatibility and updates
The target specification defines the protocol-generation support window. Reject unknown/incompatible interpretations clearly, preserve valid permitted playback and report actual versus desired versions. Updates require controlled distribution, a configurable window, qualified installation/recovery and verified rollback behavior. Never assume an untested app/data downgrade is safe. Urgent security exceptions must be explicitly reviewed and communicated; no store, installer or update library is selected here.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Governing controls and implementation boundary
text:
Governing controls and implementation boundary
**Decided requirements:** HTTPS, secure established authentication, server-side authorization and tenant isolation, separate device identities with revocable credentials, relevant audit, validated private media, recoverable backups, structured redacted telemetry and controlled updates. These are acceptance obligations; the foundation runtime alone does not implement tenant/device security.
Apply the inherited [authentication](../security/authentication.md), [authorization](../security/authorization.md), [data classification](../security/data-classification.md), [retention](../security/data-retention.md), [redaction](../security/telemetry-redaction.md), [secrets](../security/secrets-management.md), [production access](../security/production-access.md), and [error handling](../architecture/error-handling.md) policies. Do not invent cryptography, token schemes or password implementations. Accepted [ADR-0012](../adr/0012-verify-jwt-access-tokens-at-the-first-api-boundary.md) remains authoritative for human API access-token verification; a provider, full session lifecycle and device-authentication design are pending.

heading: Actors and authorization
text:
Actors and authorization
The named actor categories are **decided**; this initial capability allocation is **proposed** for review under D-02/PH-11. Roles are not yet implemented permission identifiers.

Boundary to preserve

No automatic unrestricted customer-content browsing or impersonation; support elevation must be attributable, scoped and audited

Cannot administer another company or grant platform authority

Check membership, tenant ownership, branch scope, operation and current resource state on the server. Cover detail/list/search/count/export, uploads/downloads/previews, manifests, synchronization reports and caches. Scope background work and reference validation as carefully as direct requests. Never trust a caller's tenant/role field or rely solely on a hidden button.
The first product slice needs both allow/deny tests with two companies and differently scoped branches, including resource-ID substitution, mixed-tenant references, stale membership, privilege escalation, unsafe assignment and bulk operations. Custom catalog fields, schema definitions, record/media bindings and imported layouts are subject to the same enforcement. Physical tenant enforcement remains proposed under ADR-0018.
Designated price saves automatically publish affected published content under completed PH-09. Server authorization must cover both the data mutation and its distribution targets; a draft-only edit permission cannot silently acquire publication power. Expose that consequence in the editing flow, keep unrelated drafts unpublished and audit actor/scope/revision/outcome. The detailed permission matrix remains PH-11; automatic work cannot bypass branch or tenant checks.

text:
Pairing and device lifecycle
Pairing codes must be temporary, single-use, bound to the requesting device/enrollment intent, rate-limited and safe under concurrent claims; length/entropy/expiry are reviewed protocol decisions, not values invented in this plan. The claiming human must already be authorized for the destination company/branch. A displayed code is not an enduring device credential.
Use established platform protections for local credential storage, protected transport, rotation/revocation and controlled updates. Keep raw codes, tokens, signing material and credential-bearing links out of logs, public errors, screenshots and support bundles. Rooted/stolen or physically accessible devices are a separate exposure risk; offline playback cannot guarantee protection against a person who controls the hardware.
Revocation denies future server access; an unreachable device cannot receive an immediate wipe or new policy. [Selected release policies](release-policies.md#offline-authorization-and-clock-trust) and AT-15/AT-16 define the bounded authorization/clock behavior, distinct pending/confirmed erasure and verified cleanup/reset before another tenant's pairing. Credential/time-estimation mechanisms and hardware verification remain D-03/D-07. Do not claim instant remote erasure of cached data. No general remote shell or unattended support access is part of the release.

Audit and operational telemetry
Classification inherited from contained fields; generally private
Attributable actions, incident investigation and reliability; bounded independent retention
The release does not require patient records, biometrics, card data, surveillance footage or other sensitive personal records. Configurable fields and a weekly-agenda view do not authorize collecting them; use public/synthetic events for examples and qualification. Prevent unsupported data collection and agree customer upload restrictions, purpose, retention/deletion/export, privacy notices, customer/operator responsibilities and incident handling under [PH-13](human-actions.md#ph-13). LGPD and international privacy applicability require qualified review against actual operation; this is not a legal compliance certification.
Catalog/layout imports and values are untrusted data. Validate type/size/reference/schema evolution and prevent arbitrary code, SQL, executable markup or implicit external fetches. Rendering text or selecting a typed reference must not expose private record/media access. Operational report/history defaults in the acceptance targets do not decide legal or security-audit retention.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Media and audit protections
text:
Media and audit protections
Validate type using trustworthy inspection as well as declared metadata; define size, dimensions, duration and supported codec/container bounds, safe names/paths and parser isolation. Arbitrary user uploads are not executable content. Malware/content inspection and processing tools are pending risk decisions; no unvalidated transcoding framework is selected. Download authorization must cover tenant/device/retained-publication access and prevent public object exposure.
Audit relevant membership/role changes, device pair/revoke/reassignment, publication and important media lifecycle operations with attributable actor, scope, target, time and outcome. Do not use sampled debug logs as the sole durable audit mechanism. Decide integrity, retention, authorized audit access and failure handling before implementing the affected actions. Expected failures have safe explicit errors; unexpected failures remain observable under the inherited error contract.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Internationalization
text:
Internationalization
**Decided:** engineering source/identifiers/docs remain English; interfaces must be designed for localization, initially `pt-BR` and `en-US`. Do not put user-interface copy inside domain rules or use translated labels as persisted identifiers. No i18n library is selected yet.
Separate message keys/parameters from display text, including validation, accessibility labels, device setup and operational states. Translate safely without permitting arbitrary executable markup.
Present dates, times and numeric values using the selected locale. User-facing server errors need stable codes and safe parameters rather than coupling business rules to localized sentences.
Explicitly model timezone per branch/device. PH-09 selected [calendar/DST behavior](release-policies.md#time-and-scheduling), device override then deliberately selected branch timezone and per-target local business time. Never inherit host timezone. D-06/D-10 implement matching preview/player fixtures and qualify trusted-time behavior against AT-16; business policy is no longer an unanswered PH-09 choice.
Locale is independent of timezone, currency and country. Monetary catalog fields use explicit currency and exact representation with scoped branch overrides; precision/rounding contracts must be reviewed before schema implementation. Formatting is not conversion; no automatic exchange service is selected. A generic catalog is not required to contain money fields.
Localize units and numeric presentation without changing persisted semantic meaning. Currency, decimal/grouping separators, longer translations and different date conventions must be tested.
Define the Android schedule/time interpretation with the same contract fixtures as backend preview. Changing UI language must not change actual publication timing or tenant permission.
The first product UI slice should establish this boundary. Localization of the existing foundation shell is not performed in this task.

title: Alerting
heading: Alerting
text:
Alerting
This policy owns actionable alert conditions, severity, ownership, notification, and rule maintenance. [Metrics](metrics.md) owns measurement semantics; [incident response](../security/incident-response.md) owns incidents; [runbooks](../runbooks/README.md) own executable procedures. Alerts direct human or automated attention to a condition requiring action, rather than notifying merely because a signal exists.

title: Alerting
heading: Current scope
text:
Current scope
[ADR-0010](../adr/0010-establish-observability-logging-tracing-metrics-and-error-reporting-strategy.md) leaves the observability backend and deployment alerting infrastructure application-specific. The API has runtime telemetry and health checks, but no deployed alert rules, paging provider, on-call schedule, service objectives, or alert-as-code validation. This policy establishes constraints for introducing them; it does not authorize or start deployment work.
Provider, severity taxonomy, channels/escalation, SLO tooling and burn-rate thresholds, ownership metadata, maintenance windows, and rollback integration must follow actual team structure, topology, service expectations, and operational tooling. Significant architectural choices require an ADR. Do not invent deployment thresholds or missing capabilities to fill documentation.

title: Alerting
heading: Alert severity and response
text:
Alert severity and response
Use a small consistent severity model whose levels determine response time, channel, and escalation. Severity reflects impact and urgency, not alarming wording or one HTTP error. The following is conceptual guidance, not a selected severity taxonomy or response-time commitment.
Impact
Appropriate response
Major outage, data integrity/security risk, critical workflow unavailable, widespread failure without recovery
May require immediate paging.
Substantial degradation, increasing failure rate, important dependency failure, or backlog threatening objectives
Prompt action; page only when it cannot safely wait.
Limited degradation with workaround or actionable capacity trend
Business-hours notification or owned work item may fit.
Noncritical trend, deprecation use, or an isolated automatically recovered instance
Dashboard/periodic review; avoid competing with urgent alerts.
Paging is for a reliable condition requiring action before the next normal working period, with an authorized recipient who can mitigate it. Safe automatic recovery may eliminate the need to page. Critical unacknowledged alerts need an escalation path; broadcasting to everyone is not ownership. Email suits slower risks; critical incidents must not rely only on easily missed chat notifications.
Production and non-production must be distinguishable. Staging may notify development/release owners; local development should not generate operational alerts, and ordinary test failures should fail CI rather than page production responders.

title: Alerting
heading: Symptom-based alerting
text:
Symptom-based alerting
Prefer evidence of user/service impact: valid requests failing, latency objectives violated, work missing deadlines, or a critical operation unavailable. Cause metrics support investigation. Preventive cause alerts are appropriate when a known risk, meaningful response window, and effective action can prevent impact, such as full storage, expiring certificates, recovery-threatening replication lag, or an undrainable queue.
An alert must answer what action follows. If none is required, use a dashboard, metric, log, periodic review, or ticket as appropriate. Before adding a signal, inspect existing symptom alerts for the same incident. Do not page separately on every error, restart, unready replica, retry, short circuit-breaker transition, or arbitrary resource percentage.
Prefer safe, understood, verifiable automatic recovery; notify when it fails, repeats excessively, threatens capacity/redundancy, or leaves meaningful impact. Unique/stateful instances and data-risk failures may justify instance-level alerts even when stateless replicated services use service-level aggregation.

title: Alerting
heading: Alert ownership and context
text:
Alert ownership and context
Every alert must identify an owner able and authorized to act. Ownership can follow service, domain, application, or infrastructure responsibility. Shared dependency failures need coordinated response across infrastructure and affected application owners, not independent competing investigations.
Use stable semantic names describing the condition; keep volatile thresholds in configuration. Names, ownership, severity, service, environment, and signal type should be machine-readable where tooling supports it. Do not group alerts primarily by arbitrary message text or use high-cardinality personal data in queries.
A concise notification should explain impact, duration, current value versus threshold/objective, release when relevant, owner, and first investigation step. Link directly to useful dashboards/runbooks and safe trace/error references where available. Investigators should be able to connect the condition to affected service/release, metrics, error groups, traces, and recovery guidance.
Notifications must contain only safe operational context. Chat/paging access may be broader than production telemetry: keep detailed evidence in authorized systems, and never include credentials, raw payloads, personal data, or restricted identifiers. Follow [telemetry redaction](../security/telemetry-redaction.md) and [production access](../security/production-access.md), including for AI investigation.
Acknowledgement assigns response ownership; it does not resolve the condition. Alert resolution means the triggering condition cleared, not that the root cause is permanently fixed or the incident is closed. [Incident response](../security/incident-response.md) determines proportional coordination and closure based on impact, duration, data/security risk, and involved owners. Incidents may arise without an automated alert, and not every alert becomes an incident.

title: Alerting
heading: Thresholds, windows, and missing data
text:
Thresholds, windows, and missing data
Thresholds require evidence: real service expectations/SLOs, capacity/safe limits, deadlines, known operational requirements, or an appropriate historical baseline. Never invent arbitrary availability percentages or round resource thresholds. Dynamic/anomaly rules add false-positive risk; use them when simpler rules cannot express the condition effectively.
Persistence windows, hysteresis, and aggregation can reduce flapping. Choose duration from time-to-impact; corruption, all replicas unavailable, or security breach indicators may require immediate action. Slow risks should allow useful remediation lead time. A pending period is a deliberate delay, not a universal requirement. Recovery thresholds/notifications should represent actual improvement.
Define missing-data semantics explicitly: no traffic, dead service, failed exporter, and renamed metric are different states. Absence must not silently equal healthy zero. Observability pipeline impairment can justify an alert when diagnostic capability is materially lost; avoid one page per backend hiccup. Telemetry failure should not normally break business operations, but prolonged blindness can require intervention.

title: Alerting
heading: SLO-based alerting
text:
SLO-based alerting
When meaningful SLOs exist, prefer user-impact measurements from accurate SLIs. Define eligible/successful requests or events and distinguish technical failures from expected client/business outcomes. An incorrect denominator makes the alert misleading.
An error budget is the permitted failure allowance over the objective window. Burn rate describes consumption relative to the rate that would exhaust that allowance over the window: a rate of one follows that planned rate. Fast burn over short windows may require paging; slower sustained burn may justify less urgent work. Short and longer confirmation windows can reduce transient false positives. Select formulas, thresholds, windows, and slow-burn coverage only against actual objectives and validate behavior.
Infrastructure alerts can coexist with SLO alerts when they detect distinct preventive risks. A service objective should not be fabricated to justify an existing metric threshold.

title: Alerting
heading: Choosing the signal
text:
Choosing the signal
Surface
Decision rule
Error rate
Use a meaningful denominator and enough traffic. Low-volume services may need minimum counts, longer windows, or absolute failure conditions. Expected business declines are not availability failures.
Latency
Prefer distributions or objective thresholds to averages alone; tail percentiles such as p99 can be unstable at low volume.
Queue
Combine age, arrival/processing throughput, drain capacity, deadlines, and backlog. Depth alone does not establish impact. Dead letters matter when important work has exhausted recovery; one malformed noncritical item may not page.
Dependency
Measure the application's observed impact; a provider status page is supporting context. Coordinate shared-provider incidents.
Database
Consider sustained latency, deadlock surges, unavailability, recovery-threatening lag, or pool saturation causing waits/timeouts/failures. Do not alert on every slow-query fingerprint prematurely.
CPU/memory
Use demonstrated saturation, latency, lost headroom, unexpected growth, eviction/restart, or known failure limits. High healthy utilization alone is insufficient.
Storage, certificates, expiring secrets
Give enough preventive lead time. Prefer automated renewal/rotation where safe rather than relying only on notifications.
Backups/restore
Distinguish one retryable attempt from recovery objectives at risk. Successful backup creation does not establish recoverability; restore verification can have separate signals.
Migration
Production failure must immediately become visible to deployment systems. Human paging depends on release state, impact, and safe recovery.
Readiness/liveness
Assess ready capacity, redundancy, duration, traffic, and restart loops. A healthy pool should usually recover one stateless replica automatically.
Error tracker
New actionable issues, regressions, fatal crashes, or frequency changes may matter. Unsupported client-extension noise does not deserve the same response as a critical backend workflow failure.
Security/audit
Security-specific detection/escalation follows incident policy. Recording a privileged action does not automatically require notification; suspicious or policy-significant conditions may.
Quota/cost
For quotas consider consumption, growth, and time until reset. Reliable trends can support preventive work; budget notifications are not automatically reliability incidents.

title: Alerting
heading: Deduplication, maintenance, and deployment
text:
Deduplication, maintenance, and deployment
Aggregate identical replica failures into the service condition. A primary symptom can page while related dependency signals remain supporting context. Parent-condition suppression must not hide unrelated independent failures.
Maintenance suppression must be explicit, owned, scoped, and time-bounded. Do not permanently mute alerts or disable all alerting during every deployment; releases are when regressions often appear. Suppress only known expected behavior for its actual window, and correlate alerts with recent deployment/release annotations where practical.
Canary comparison and automated rollback remain deployment capabilities, not foundation defaults. Any automation needs high-confidence signals, clear rollback safety, bounded execution, and auditability. Never attach noisy alerts to destructive automated actions. Canary error/latency/critical-success comparisons must follow an actual release policy.

title: Alerting
heading: Rule lifecycle and noisy alert review
text:
Rule lifecycle and noisy alert review
Prefer version-controlled, reviewed, reproducible rules where tooling supports them. Provider-side manual rules may be acceptable during early experimentation; long-term critical detection should be reproducible from repository-controlled configuration. Review critical changes like production code.
Validate query syntax, metric/label existence, expressions, metadata, and runbook links with available tools. Critical rules need meaningful healthy/unhealthy/recovery evidence through query fixtures, rule tests, or safe staging simulation. Document unavailable checks rather than claiming verification.
High-severity alerts should have useful runbooks when practical. Prioritize recurring high-impact gaps. A runbook should identify actual signals/queries, common causes, safe mitigation, verification, and escalation rather than merely saying "check logs". Follow [runbook authoring](../runbooks/authoring.md); a runbook does not grant operational authority.
Treat chronic noise as a defect. Review signal, threshold, duration, flapping, expected behavior, ownership, automatic recovery, duplicate coverage, severity/channel, and whether automation or a root-cause fix removes recurring manual work. Raising thresholds, permanent muting, or deletion without understanding the signal is not a fix. Before removing an established alert, identify its original purpose, replacement coverage, and dependent runbooks.
As operational needs grow, assess pages per incident, false positives, alerts with no action, acknowledgement time, and repeated noise. Measurements should guide improvements rather than create another alert stream.

title: Alerting
heading: New alert checklist
text:
New alert checklist
Before creating or changing an alert, establish:
The condition, actual impact/risk, required action, urgency, and authorized owner.
A stable reliable signal, meaningful denominator/missing-data semantics, justified threshold, persistence/recovery behavior, and representative tests.
Whether safe recovery, an existing symptom alert, aggregation, or a work item better addresses the condition.
Safe concise context, correct environment/channel/escalation, and useful investigation/runbook links.
For paging: why action cannot wait, whether the recipient can mitigate it, and how duplicate pages and unacknowledged incidents are handled.
For SLO/resource alerts: real objective/eligible population or safe capacity/deadline, expected impact, and sufficient lead time for the response.
An alert is not ready if its impact, action, ownership, or threshold justification cannot be explained. Available repository checks are listed in [validation](../validation.md); deployment-specific alert tooling remains conditional.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Error Reporting
text:
Error Reporting
This policy owns unexpected-failure capture, diagnostic context, grouping, and issue triage. [Error handling](../architecture/error-handling.md) owns application failure semantics; the [public error contract](../api/error-contract.md) owns responses. Error tracking complements logs, traces, and metrics; it is neither an audit ledger nor a business analytics store.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Current implementation and accepted direction
text:
Current implementation and accepted direction
[ADR-0010](../adr/0010-establish-observability-logging-tracing-metrics-and-error-reporting-strategy.md) establishes central error handling, Pino logs, and OpenTelemetry correlation as the foundation. A dedicated error-reporting provider is optional and deployment-specific. No global tracker, provider SDK, source-map upload pipeline, browser crash integration, or issue-routing service is implemented. These capabilities must follow real application needs; do not add a generic provider abstraction without an application responsibility.
The API [error boundary](../../apps/api/src/app.ts) reports one `unhandled_request_error` with a stable error ID and [bounded safe diagnostics](../../apps/api/src/error-diagnostics.ts), then returns a safe [`INTERNAL_ERROR` envelope](../../apps/api/src/errors.ts). Only allowlisted error types/codes and repository-owned frame locations are retained; raw messages, arbitrary stacks, and cause objects are excluded. Authentication infrastructure failure receives a safe 503 and `authentication_unavailable` diagnostic. [Startup](../../apps/api/src/main.ts) catches configuration, initialization, connection, and listen failures, attempts bounded cleanup, and emits a fixed safe fallback record if the logger does not yet exist. [Observability](observability.md) owns current correlation and release context.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Expected vs unexpected
text:
Expected vs unexpected
Classification is semantic, not determined by an exception type or HTTP status.
Failure
Reporting treatment
Modeled validation, invalid credentials, permission denial, not-found, rate limit, domain rejection, or optimistic concurrency conflict
Normal error contract; useful aggregate metrics, safe operational/security logs, and required audit events. Do not create tracker issues by default.
Missing required internal state, broken invariant, programming defect, unexpected provider shape, or authentication subsystem crash
Unexpected: surface safe diagnostic evidence at the owning boundary.
Provider business decline
Expected provider/domain outcome; distinguish it from provider availability failure.
Dependency outage or exhausted retries
Operational failure; report the logical failed operation where appropriate, not an issue per retry.
Transient failure/deadlock recovered by retry
Prefer attempt/outcome metrics, traces, and bounded warnings. Repeated or unrecoverable failures must remain visible.
Client offline state, cancelled navigation, unsupported extension, or external script failure
Classify against product behavior and ownership; use deliberate noise filters rather than treating every event as an application defect.
A specific security or operational requirement may justify capturing an otherwise expected outcome; document the reason and bounded scope. Sampling does not replace correct classification.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Report once
text:
Report once
Each execution model needs an authoritative final boundary: HTTP handler, job runner, consumer wrapper, scheduler, CLI entry point, or client error boundary. Capture an unexpected failure once there. Intermediate layers may translate, wrap, enrich, and preserve cause without duplicate capture. If a catch intentionally consumes an unexpected failure, that layer owns reporting or another explicit way to surface it. Never silently lose it.
Prefer the actual exception or an equivalent safe structured representation over a generic string. Preserve meaningful type, internal-safe message, stack, cause chain, stable code, and diagnostic metadata where supported and permitted. Sanitization must precede export; preserving a cause never authorizes recursively serializing arbitrary exception attachments. SDK/ORM/database errors can contain credentials, request/response bodies, query values, or connection details.
Fatal startup/process failures should produce a safe diagnostic where possible even if the tracker cannot initialize. Uncaught failures that leave process state unsafe require safe termination; capture does not make continued execution safe. Fatal and short-lived processes may need a bounded best-effort flush, never indefinite shutdown waiting. Follow [lifecycle and error handling](../architecture/error-handling.md).
Client error boundaries, when introduced, should capture unexpected rendering/runtime errors, show safe fallback UI, and preserve useful correlation. Recovery must be intentional and must not conceal persistent broken state. Framework boundaries do not capture every browser rejection, resource failure, native crash, or hang; choose platform-specific coverage only where required.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Public vs internal error
text:
Public vs internal error
Keep public messages/codes separate from internal diagnostic evidence. Internal stacks and provider details must not leak through responses. An opaque `errorId` can connect a support reference to an occurrence, logs, and trace; it never grants telemetry access. Support staff and AI investigators need the same authorization as any other production investigator.
Capture the producing service/application, environment, deployed release, and semantic operation. Release identity must identify the actual artifact, remain correlatable after rollback, and not be confused with API, SDK, or database version. Production and non-production must be distinguishable. Meaningful tracker regression analysis requires release metadata.
Include active trace/span and request correlation where available, preferably through infrastructure rather than manual copying. Follow [logging's correlation convention](logging.md#current-implementation-and-contract); public API field names are a separate contract. Request IDs remain useful when tracing is sampled. Background work can add safe job/event identity, type/consumer, and attempt, never the entire payload. Stable error codes and bounded semantic categories may help investigation; arbitrary messages are not error codes.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Context and capture safety
text:
Context and capture safety
[Telemetry redaction](../security/telemetry-redaction.md) and [data classification](../security/data-classification.md) govern every field, including automatic SDK capture. Use minimum explicit safe projections. If context cannot be sanitized confidently, drop it. Never intentionally send `RESTRICTED` data; provider-side filters are defense in depth.
Indexed tags must be stable, bounded, and safe, such as service/environment/operation/code/provider. High-cardinality request, trace, user, resource, and job IDs belong in permitted non-indexed context when provider indexing costs warrant it. Context still needs size/nesting limits and a diagnostic purpose.
Prefer opaque actor/tenant IDs to names, email, phone, or tenant metadata. Extra personal data requires an explicit approved need. Anonymous session IDs require safe semantics and bounded retention. Device/OS/app/locale metadata should be minimized; unnecessary IP collection and precise geolocation should be disabled/minimized. Do not indiscriminately collect desktop paths, usernames, or machine names.
Do not attach complete requests, responses, user/domain/ORM objects, configuration, provider payloads, user content, or application state. Automatic request capture must omit bodies, authorization, cookies, and query values by default; response-body capture is disabled by default. Environment capture is disabled: only explicitly allowlisted safe configuration metadata may be attached.
Never construct exception messages containing credentials or connection strings. Keep dynamic IDs out of message text where a safe separate field provides the same diagnostic value and better grouping.
Breadcrumb buffers must be bounded and represent recent safe navigation, interaction categories, dependency calls, or state transitions. Review automatic console/network/DOM capture before use. Prefer method, normalized route, status, and duration; exclude typed content, payloads, credentials, sensitive query strings, and unnecessary resource IDs.
Attachments are disabled or used only with particular caution; never upload arbitrary diagnostics automatically. Screenshots require explicit classification, consent, access, and redaction rules. Session replay requires privacy/security review and is not a default. Automatic stack-frame local-variable capture is disabled unless a safe mechanism is proven.
Production tracker access follows [least privilege](../security/production-access.md), including vendor support access. [Retention and deletion](../security/data-retention.md) apply to providers storing personal data. A suspected telemetry leak follows [incident response](../security/incident-response.md): contain collection, determine affected events/providers, rotate exposed secrets where applicable, remove accessible leaked data where possible, fix the source, and add regression protection.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Grouping and fingerprint checklist
text:
Grouping and fingerprint checklist
Group occurrences by the underlying defect. Prefer provider defaults until evidence shows over-grouping of different causes or under-grouping of one defect. Ordinary deployments/line shifts should not unnecessarily split one issue. Dynamic identifiers, generated paths, and arbitrary provider messages can make grouping unstable.
Before adding a custom fingerprint, identify the defect, occurrences that belong together, failures that must remain separate, and how behavior will be validated. Values must be stable, bounded, semantic, and non-sensitive: category, operation, stable provider code, or exception class may fit. Request/user/resource IDs, email, and raw messages must not be fingerprint inputs. Give material custom grouping logic an owner and tests; avoid manual fingerprints on every error.
Deliberate filters can remove known non-actionable extension/environment/cancellation noise. Prefer stable evidence over fragile message substrings. Significant ignore rules need a reason, owner, scope, and reviewability; do not broadly ignore an exception class without understanding other failures it represents. Earlier filtering reduces privacy risk/cost but must not hide important defects.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Source map checklist
text:
Source map checklist
Build transformations must not make required production diagnostics unusable. When source maps, native symbols, or mapping files are needed:
Generate them reproducibly and associate them with the exact deployed artifact, release/build, and platform. Incorrect maps are misleading.
Define trusted storage/upload and access explicitly. Do not accidentally publish application source because a tracker needs it.
Make upload/missing-artifact failures visible in release validation when diagnostics depend on them.
Verify useful stack resolution against the actual artifact; include bounded shutdown/flush behavior for short-lived crash reporting where applicable.
Native crash/hang/ANR and mobile/desktop symbolication pipelines remain conditional on selected platforms. Introducing them does not permit unrestricted device or environment capture.

title: Error Reporting
heading: Volume and provider failure
text:
Volume and provider failure
Bound buffers, event sizes, export waits, CPU/memory/network use, and provider quotas. A failure storm must not amplify the application outage. Rate limiting, local/collector deduplication, or sampling can preserve issue existence, representative context, and frequency estimates where possible; give critical or rare failures higher retention priority. Understand provider event, attachment, indexing, and retention limits and degrade safely when reached.
Capture should normally be buffered, bounded, and non-blocking. An unavailable exporter must not normally fail business operations. Emit bounded fallback logs/metrics for capture loss or export failure without recursively reporting the tracker's own failure through itself. Development may use an isolated integration but must not trigger production incidents; ordinary test exceptions belong in CI, with test exporters or isolated environments for integration verification.
